items.expected: Chemically mapped, validated first-stage dihydrophenanthrene candidates recover the source-reference ordering IS1 below IS2. The source separation is 9.9 kcal/mol; no magnitude tolerance exists, so this item scores the supported ordering from a quantitative same-composition free-energy comparison, not an exact 9.9 match. Never compare absolute energies of different hydrogen inventories.

Independent computed orbital or equivalent site-resolved electronic/structural evidence supports the first closure site corresponding to C1 over C2 of 1-cis. The source shows greater LUMO density and the relevant relative phase pattern at C1. Absolute orbital phase/color is arbitrary; evidence must discriminate physical forming-bond sites, not merely restate energy ranking. The source phase description is qualitative; local two-point samples do not establish all nodal features. An equivalent physical site explanation passes without requiring exact orbital colors or author labels.

Starting from the chemically mapped oxidized first-stage intermediate IS3, compare valid sequential candidates and recover IS4 below IS5. The source 11.3 kcal/mol separation is context without a calibrated magnitude tolerance. Use equal-composition, common-definition free energies and establish sequential connectivity.

Computed orbital or equivalent independent site-resolved evidence for the first-stage oxidized scaffold supports the second closure at source C3 rather than C4. The source LUMO topology supports that assignment; numerical energy ordering alone does not earn this separate electronic-discrimination item.

items.statement: Chemical rationale for the sequential oxidative cyclization route
items.expected: Explain why the supported continuation is cyclization followed by aromatization before the next cyclization, rather than merely accumulating two unrearomatized closures. Use mapped hydrogen-accounted structures and comparable calculations to support the chemical inference (source IS1→IS3→IS4, with high-lying same-inventory bis-dihydro alternatives IS6/IS7). Do not require author labels or claim a balanced oxidation free energy from subtracting different hydrogen inventories. A physically equivalent supported sequence passes; endpoint stability alone is not proof of reaction rate or excited-state exclusivity. For this bounded endpoint/site rationale, mapped hydrogen-accounted connectivity and appropriate same-composition endpoint comparisons do not require a separate balanced oxidation free energy, explicit iodine calculation or reaction barrier. Evidence obligations follow the actual claim: a quantitative oxidation-energy assertion needs balanced reactant/product reference evidence, and a kinetic-order assertion needs corresponding pathway or kinetic evidence. Missing evidence necessary for the submitted inference fails that claim; omission of unclaimed oxidation energetics alone does not.
